es.summary: La RCI es la condición en la que el feto no alcanza su potencial de crecimiento, generalmente por insuficiencia placentaria. Se diagnostica cuando el peso estimado está por debajo del percentil 10 para la edad gestacional.
key_points: Peso fetal <10.º percentil o <2 desviaciones estándar.
Insuficiencia placentaria es la causa más frecuente.
Factores maternos como hipertensión, tabaquismo y malnutrición aumentan el riesgo.
Complicaciones neonatales incluyen prematuridad, hipoglucemia y retraso del desarrollo.
El manejo incluye vigilancia materno‑fetal intensiva y posible parto prematuro.

pathophysiology: Placenta insuficiente reduce oxígeno y nutrientes al feto.
El feto adapta el flujo sanguíneo, priorizando órganos vitales.
Disminución de la síntesis de IGF‑1 y hormona del crecimiento fetal.
Crecimiento lineal y ponderal se ralentiza, resultando en bajo peso.
risk_factors: Tabaquismo y consumo de alcohol o drogas.
Desnutrición materna o bajo índice de masa corporal.
Embarazo múltiple y edad materna <18 o >35 años.
signs_symptoms: Altura uterina menor al esperado para la edad gestacional.
Ecografía: peso estimado <10.º percentil, flujo Doppler anómalo.
diagnostics: Doppler de arteria umbilical y vena cava.
Laboratorio materno: hemoglobina, glucosa, pruebas de infección.
treatment: Control estricto de la presión arterial materna.
Suplementación nutricional y vitaminas (ácido fólico, hierro).
Corticoides antenatos para maduración pulmonar si se anticipa parto prematuro.
Reposo relativo y vigilancia de la actividad fetal.
Planificación de parto temprano si hay deterioro fetal.
complications: Parto prematuro y bajo peso al nacer.
Hipoglucemia neonatal y dificultad para mantener la temperatura.
Retraso neurocognitivo y motor a largo plazo.
nursing_care: Monitorear presión arterial y peso materno diariamente.
Evaluar movimientos fetales y registrar altura uterina.
Preparar al recién nacido para cuidados de NICU (termómetro, balanza, glucosa).
Mantener ambiente cálido (incubadora o cuna con calefacción).
Coordinar pruebas de laboratorio y ecografías según indicación.
patient_teaching: Importancia de asistir a todas las consultas prenatales.
Adoptar una dieta balanceada rica en proteínas y calorías.
Evitar tabaco, alcohol y drogas ilícitas.
Reconocer signos de trabajo de parto prematuro (contracciones, pérdida de líquido).
Instruir sobre la lactancia temprana y la monitorización de la glucosa neonatal.

care_plans.diagnosis: Riesgo de déficit de volumen de líquidos
outcomes: Balance hídrico mantenido: ingesta y salida de líquidos equilibradas en 48 h
Peso estable dentro de ±5 % del peso esperado en 72 h

interventions.action: Registrar ingesta y salida de líquidos cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Permite detectar rápidamente desequilibrios de volumen

interventions.action: Pesar al recién nacido diariamente a la misma hora
interventions.rationale: El peso es indicador sensible de déficit o exceso de líquidos

interventions.action: Evaluar turgencia de la piel y mucosas cada turno
interventions.rationale: Identifica signos tempranos de deshidratación

interventions.action: Mantener ambiente térmico adecuado (incubadora a 36‑37 °C)
interventions.rationale: Reduce pérdidas de calor y, por ende, de líquidos

interventions.action: Fomentar la lactancia materna precoz y frecuente
interventions.rationale: La leche materna aporta fluidos y nutrientes esenciales

outcomes: Cultivos de sangre y orina negativos al día 5 de vida

interventions.action: Aplicar técnica aséptica al manipular al neonato
interventions.rationale: Previene la introducción de microorganismos patógenos

interventions.action: Monitorizar temperatura cada 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detecta fiebre temprana, signo de infección

interventions.action: Observar enrojecimiento, edema o secreción en sitios de catéteres
interventions.rationale: Identifica signos locales de infección

interventions.action: Lavado de manos antes y después de cada contacto con el bebé
interventions.rationale: Reduce la transmisión de gérmenes

interventions.action: Educar a los padres sobre higiene de manos y cuidado del cordón umbilical
interventions.rationale: Fomenta prácticas que disminuyen el riesgo de infección en casa

en.summary: IUGR is the condition in which the fetus does not reach its growth potential, usually due to placental insufficiency. It is diagnosed when the estimated weight is below the 10th percentile for gestational age.
key_points: Fetal weight <10th percentile or <2 standard deviations.
Placental insufficiency is the most common cause.
Maternal factors such as hypertension, smoking, and malnutrition increase risk.
Neonatal complications include prematurity, hypoglycemia, and developmental delay.
Management includes intensive maternal‑fetal monitoring and possible preterm delivery.

pathophysiology: Placental insufficiency reduces oxygen and nutrients to the fetus.
The fetus adapts blood flow, prioritizing vital organs.
Decreased synthesis of IGF‑1 and fetal growth hormone.
Linear and weight growth slows, resulting in low birth weight.
risk_factors: Smoking and consumption of alcohol or drugs.
Maternal malnutrition or low body mass index.
Multiple gestation and maternal age <18 or >35 years.
signs_symptoms: Uterine height less than expected for gestational age.
Ultrasound: estimated weight <10th percentile, abnormal Doppler flow.
diagnostics: Umbilical artery and vena cava Doppler.
Maternal labs: hemoglobin, glucose, infection tests.
treatment: Strict control of maternal blood pressure.
Nutritional supplementation and vitamins (folic acid, iron).
Antepartum corticosteroids for lung maturation if preterm delivery anticipated.
Relative rest and fetal activity monitoring.
Early delivery planning if fetal deterioration.
complications: Preterm birth and low birth weight.
Neonatal hypoglycemia and difficulty maintaining temperature.
nursing_care: Monitor maternal blood pressure and weight daily.
Assess fetal movements and record uterine height.
Prepare the newborn for NICU care (thermometer, scale, glucose).
Maintain a warm environment (incubator or heated crib).
Coordinate laboratory tests and ultrasounds as ordered.
patient_teaching: Importance of attending all prenatal visits.
Adopt a balanced diet rich in protein and calories.
Avoid tobacco, alcohol, and illicit drugs.
Recognize signs of preterm labor (contractions, fluid loss).
Educate on early breastfeeding and neonatal glucose monitoring.

outcomes: Hydrostatic balance maintained: intake and output balanced within 48 h
Weight stable within ±5 % of expected weight in 72 h

interventions.action: Record intake and output every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Allows rapid detection of volume imbalances

interventions.action: Weigh the newborn daily at the same time
interventions.rationale: Weight is a sensitive indicator of fluid deficit or excess

interventions.action: Assess skin and mucous turgor each shift
interventions.rationale: Identifies early signs of dehydration

interventions.action: Maintain adequate thermal environment (incubator at 36‑37 °C)
interventions.rationale: Reduces heat loss and, therefore, fluid loss

interventions.action: Encourage early and frequent breastfeeding
interventions.rationale: Breast milk provides essential fluids and nutrients

outcomes: Blood and urine cultures negative by day 5 of life

interventions.action: Apply aseptic technique when handling the neonate
interventions.rationale: Prevents introduction of pathogenic microorganisms

interventions.action: Monitor temperature every 4 h
interventions.rationale: Detects early fever, a sign of infection

interventions.action: Observe for redness, edema, or discharge at catheter sites
interventions.rationale: Identifies local infection signs

interventions.action: Wash hands before and after each contact with the baby
interventions.rationale: Reduces transmission of germs

interventions.action: Educate parents on hand hygiene and umbilical cord care
interventions.rationale: Promotes practices that reduce infection risk at home

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Problems with the placenta, the organ that brings oxygen and nutrients to the baby

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Hypertension that is present prior to pregnancy or before 20 weeks’ gestation or that persists 20 weeks following delivery is called chronic hypertension .

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Smoking tobacco in pregnancy has been associated with fetal growth restriction, miscarriage, prematurity, placental abruption , stillbirth, tissue damage to the fetal lungs and brain, and neurodevelopmental disorders (Chen et al., 2023; Cohen et al., 2017; Nida, 2021).

sections.risk_factors.3.quote: The CDC currently recommends HIV screening for all patients who are pregnant (CDC, 2022c), but additional screening may be indicated for high-risk populations.

sections.treatment.1.quote: Nurses should provide education on the intake of nutrients such as folic acid, iron, vitamin B12, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, and choline during pregnancy.

sections.complications.0.quote: Pregnant farm workers are at increased risk of preterm birth and having low-birth-weight infants.

sections.complications.1.quote: Diabetes, especially when glycemic control is not present prior to conception and throughout the pregnancy, is associated with an increased risk of maternal and fetal adverse outcomes, such as miscarriage, congenital anomalies, stillbirth, preeclampsia , fetal macrosomia, and neonatal hypoglycemia (American Diabetes Association [ADA], 2020).

sections.complications.2.quote: Affected Person Effects Pregnant person Preeclampsia Gestational hypertension Polyhydramnios Cesarean birth Hypoglycemia Diabetic ketoacidosis Postpartum hemorrhage Diabetic retinopathy Diabetic kidney disease Cardiac disease Neuropathy Early pregnancy loss Preterm delivery Fetus Neonatal hypoglycemia Large for gestational age/Macrosomia Fetal growth restriction Shoulder dystocia Respiratory distress syndrome Congenital malformations: Neural tube

sections.complications.3.quote: There is also a higher risk of longer-term problems, including: Delayed motor and social development Learning disabilities Certain health conditions as an adult, such as heart disease , high blood pressure , diabetes , and obesity

sections.nursing_care.4.quote: Surveillance of fetal well-being is conducted via ordered ultrasound (US) with Doppler , nonstress test (NST) , and biophysical profile (BPP) .

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: Patients should also be advised to follow a healthy diet, engage in regular physical activity, and attend all prenatal appointments.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: The nurse should teach the patient ways to reduce risks of HIV perinatal transmission, such as limiting alcohol, tobacco, and illicit drug use and avoiding unprotected intercourse.
